Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 1:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, who makes the angels messengers having wings, two or three or four. He increases in creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is competent over all things.﴾ (1)

He, the Exalted, says: Perfect gratitude is to the One worshipped, besides whom no worship is fitting and who alone it is not proper to make the object of worship of anyone else, the Creator of the seven heavens and the earth, ﴿who makes the angels messengers﴾ to whomever He wills of His servants, and concerning whatever He wills of His command and prohibition, ﴿having wings, two or three or four﴾, meaning: possessors of wings, that is, angels. Some of them have two wings, some have three wings, and some have four.

As follows:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿having wings, two or three or four﴾, he said: Some of them have two wings, some three, and some four.

The grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyyah) differed regarding the reason why mathna, thulath andruba' are not declined (with nunation), and they are a rendering of ajniha (wings), which is indefinite. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: their non-declension is because they are diverted from their original forms, for mathna is diverted from ithnayn (two), thulath from thalathah (three), and ruba' from arba'ah (four). Thus they are like 'Umar and Zufar, since this one is diverted from 'Amir to 'Umar and this one from Zafir to Zufar. Some of them recited in this regard:

"And indeed I killed you in pairs and singly, and left Marrah like yesterday's retreater..." [[The line is by Sakhr ibn 'Amr ibn al-Sharid al-Sulami. Its citation has already preceded, together with other evidences, at (4: 337) of this tafsir, so refer to it there. Abu 'Ubaydah recited it in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 201), saying: "Mathna, thulath, and ruba': their meaning is ithnayn, thalathah, and arba'ah. The grammarians claim that because it was diverted from its original form, nunation is not applied to them." End of quote.]]

Another of them said: It is not declined because it implies three and four, and this is used only in the state of counting.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: They are diverted from definiteness, because the definite article (al-) does not enter them, nor does the genitive construction (idafah). He said: If the idafah and the definite article entered them, they would be indefinite, and they are a rendering of the indefinite. He said: Likewise whatever is in the Qur'an like ﴿that you stand up for Allah in pairs or singly﴾, and likewise wahid and ahad, and what resembles them of numerals that are diverted.

* *

As for His words ﴿He increases in creation what He wills﴾:

That is His, the Blessed and Exalted's, increase in the creation of this angel with wings over another what He wills, and His decrease of another from what He loves. Likewise, this is so in all His creation: He increases in the creation of whatever He wills in what He wills, and decreases from the creation of whatever He wills what He wills. To Him belong creation and command, and to Him belong power and dominion. ﴿Indeed, Allah is competent over all things﴾ means: Indeed Allah, the Exalted, who is mighty in His remembrance, is capable of increasing what He wills of that in what He wills, and decreasing what He wills of it from whom He wills, and other things, all of them; nothing prevents Him from doing anything He, glorified and exalted, has willed.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 2:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whatever mercy Allah grants to the people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him. And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: The keys of goodness and its locks are all in His hand. So whatever good Allah opens to the people, there is none to lock it, nor to withhold it from them, for that is His command, and no one can contest His command. Likewise, whatever good He locks away from them, He does not extend it to them nor open it for them, and there is no one to open it besides Him, for all matters belong to Him and are referred to Him.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Whatever mercy Allah grants to the people﴾: i.e., of good; ﴿none can withhold it﴾: no one can restrain it. ﴿And whatever He withholds, none can release after Him﴾.

He, the Exalted, said ﴿none can withhold it﴾ using the feminine pronoun, referring back to "mercy" (rahmah), and said ﴿whatever He withholds, none can release after Him﴾ using the masculine pronoun, referring to the wording of "ma" (what), since its wording is masculine. If one uses the feminine in a place requiring the masculine according to meaning, and the masculine in a place requiring the feminine according to wording, it is permissible; but the more eloquent usage is the feminine when a word indicating its femininity appears after it, and the masculine when that is not apparent.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾:

He says: He is the Almighty in His vengeance upon whomever among His creatures He takes vengeance, by withholding His mercy and His goods from him; the All-Wise in the management of His creatures and His opening of mercy to them when opening it is righteous, and His withholding it from them when withholding it is wise.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 3:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, remember the favor of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? There is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?﴾ (35:3)

Exalted is He, says He, to the polytheists among the people of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from the Quraysh: ﴿O mankind, remember the favor of Allah﴾ which He has bestowed ﴿upon you﴾ by opening for you of His good things what He has opened, and by extending for you of livelihood what He has extended. Reflect and consider: is there any creator besides the Originator of the heavens and the earth, in whose hand are the keys of your provisions and their locks? (﴿He provides for you from the heaven and the earth﴾), so that you would worship Him rather than Him. ﴿There is no deity except Him.﴾ He says: there is no worshipped one deserving of worship except the One who originated the heavens and the earth, the Able over all things, in whose hand are the keys of all things and their treasuries, and the locks of all of that. So, O people, do not worship anything other than Him, for none other than Him is able to benefit you or harm you. So make your worship sincere to Him and single Him out for divinity. ﴿So how are you deluded?﴾ He says: In what direction are you being turned away from your Creator and your Provider, in whose hand is your benefit and harm?

As:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿so how are you deluded?﴾: the man says: "Indeed, he turns me away from such-and-such."

I have already explained the meaning of ifk (turning away, deluding) and the interpretation of His saying ﴿you are deluded﴾ earlier, with evidence sufficient to make its repetition unnecessary.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verses 4–5:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then already were messengers denied before you. And to Allah are returned [all] matters.﴾ ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is truth, so let not the worldly life deceive you, and let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah.﴾

His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: And if these polytheists among your people deny you, O Muhammad, then let that not grieve you, nor weigh heavily upon you, for that is the way of their likes among the disbelieving nations toward Allah, before them, and their denial of the messengers of Allah whom He sent to them before you. The polytheists of your people will not go beyond being like them, so they will follow their path in denying you and tread their way. ﴿And to Allah are returned the matters.﴾ His exalted remembrance says: To Allah is the return of your affair and theirs; so He will inflict punishment upon them if they do not turn back to obedience to Us in following you, acknowledging your prophethood, and accepting what you have called them to of counsel, [He will inflict] the like of what We inflicted upon their counterparts among the nations that denied their messengers before you, and [He will] deliver you and your followers from that. This is Our way with those before you concerning Our messengers and Our friends.

And the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And if they deny you, then already were messengers denied before you﴾: he consoles his Prophet, as you hear.

And His saying ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is truth﴾

His exalted remembrance says to the polytheists of Quraysh, who denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah to you, of His punishment for your persistence in disbelief in Him and your denial of His messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and His warning you of the descent of His might upon you for that, is true. So be certain of that and hasten to avert the arrival of your punishment by repentance and turning back to the obedience of Allah and belief in Him and His messenger. ﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you﴾: meaning, let not the life you are in in this world deceive you, nor your leadership by which you lord over your weak ones there, turning them away from following Muhammad and believing. ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah﴾: meaning, let not Satan deceive you concerning Allah, so that he makes you hope for vain wishes, promises you false promises from Allah, and drives you to persist in your disbelief in Allah.

As:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah﴾: he said, "The Shaytan (Satan)."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 6:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ (35:6)

He, exalted is His mention, says: ﴿Indeed, Satan﴾ whom I have forbidden you, O people, to be deceived by his delusion of you concerning God, ﴿is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy.﴾ That is: place him in your own selves in the position of an enemy toward you, and beware of him through obedience to God and by distrusting him, as you beware of your enemy whose harm you fear for your own selves. So do not obey him, and do not follow his footsteps, for he only invites his party, his partisans and those who obey him, to his obedience and to accepting from him, and to disbelief in God, ﴿that they may be among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ That is: that they may be among those who abide forever in the fire of Hell, which blazes against its people.

And the people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said concerning that.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy.﴾ "It is obligatory upon every Muslim to take him as an enemy, and his enmity is to oppose him through obedience to God." ﴿He only invites his party﴾, and his party: his allies. ﴿That they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾, i.e., that he may drive them to the Fire. This is his enmity.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾, and he said: "These are his party from among mankind." He means: those are the party of Satan, and the party (hizb) are his protégés whom he takes as allies and who take him as an ally. And he recited: ﴿Indeed, my guardian is God, who revealed the Book, and He takes charge of the righteous.﴾ (7:196)

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 7:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those who disbelieve, for them is a severe punishment, and those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ (35:7)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Those who disbelieve﴾ in God and His Messenger, ﴿for them is a punishment﴾ from God, ﴿severe﴾, and that is the punishment of the Fire.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and those who believe﴾:

He means: those who affirm God and His Messenger, and act upon what God has commanded them and refrain from what He has forbidden them, ﴿for them is forgiveness﴾ from God for their sins, ﴿and a great reward﴾, and that is Paradise.

As related:

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿for them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾: it is Paradise.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 8:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Is one to whom the evil of his deed is made attractive, so he sees it as good [equal to one who is rightly guided]? For indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let yourself go in regret over them. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾

Says He, may His remembrance be exalted: Is one whose evil deeds Satan has made appealing to him, namely acts of disobedience toward Allah and disbelief in Him, and worship of other than Him among the gods and idols, so that he sees it as good, thus considering the ugliness of it to be beautiful and supposing its repulsiveness to be fine, because Satan made it attractive to him? Your soul has gone out in regret over them, [in] sighs. Something has been omitted from the speech: "your soul has gone out in regret over them, in sighs," being sufficed by the indication of His words ﴿So do not let yourself go in regret over them, in sighs﴾ from it, and His words ﴿For indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾. He says: For indeed, Allah forsakes whom He wills from faith in Him, following you and believing you, so He leaves him astray from rectitude toward the truth in that matter, and guides whom He wills. He says: and He grants success to whom He wills for faith in Him, following you and accepting from you, so you guide him to the path of rectitude. ﴿So do not let yourself go in regret over them, in sighs﴾: He says: do not destroy yourself with grief over their misguidance and their disbelief in Allah and their denial of you.

Those of the interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Is one to whom the evil of his deed is made attractive, so he sees it as good, for indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾. Qatadah and al-Hasan said: Satan made it attractive to them. ﴿So do not let yourself go in regret over them, in sighs﴾: that is, let that not grieve you over them, for indeed Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of Allah ﴿So do not let yourself go in regret over them, in sighs﴾: "The sighs" (al-hasarat) are grief. And he recited the words of Allah ﴿Alas, my regret over what I neglected in regard to Allah﴾. The words "For indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills" occur in the place of the response (jawab), but it is actually the source of the response (manba' al-jawab), because the response is the omitted part you mentioned; so it suffices with it as a response, given its indication of the response and the meaning of the speech.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿So do not let yourself go in regret over them, in sighs﴾. The readers of the major cities (qurra' al-amsar), apart from Abu Ja'far al-Madani, read ﴿fa-la tadhhab nafsuka﴾ with a fathah on the ta' of "tadhhab" and the "nafsuka" with a dammah (nafsu-ka as subject), while Abu Ja'far read ﴿fa-la tudhhib﴾ with a dammah on the ta' of "tudhhib" and "nafsaka" with a fathah (as object), meaning: do not let you, O Muhammad, bring about the loss of your soul.

The correct recitation in our view is what the readers of the major cities hold, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾:

Says He, may His remembrance be exalted: Indeed Allah, O Muhammad, has knowledge of what these people do, whose evil deeds Satan made attractive to them, and He keeps account of it against them and recompenses them with their due reward.

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is He who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land, and We revive the earth thereby after its death. Thus is the resurrection.﴾ (35:9)

His exalted mention says: And Allah is He who sends the winds, which stir up the clouds with rain and abundant water, ﴿and We drive them to a dead land﴾, meaning: We drive them to a land barren of its people, desolate, with its ground in ruins, having neither vegetation nor crops. ﴿and We revive the earth thereby after its death﴾, meaning: We bring fertility to the land to which We drove that cloud, with its rain, after its barrenness, and We make crops grow in it after its desolation. ﴿Thus is the resurrection﴾. His exalted mention says: In this way Allah raises the dead after they have decayed in their graves, and gives them life after their annihilation, just as We revived this land with rain after its death.

The people of ta'wil have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: Abu al-Za'ra' narrated to us, from Abdullah, who said: Between the two blasts there will be what Allah wills, and there is none of the children of Adam but that some of him is in the earth. He said: Then Allah will send water from beneath the Throne, like the semen of a man, and their bodies and flesh will grow from it, just as the earth grows from moist soil. Then he recited: ﴿And Allah is He who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land…﴾ to His words ﴿Thus is the resurrection.﴾ He said: Then an angel with the Trumpet will stand between heaven and earth and blow into it, and every soul will go forth to its body and enter it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿And Allah is He who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds﴾. He said: He sends the winds, and they drive the clouds, and Allah revives this dead land with this water. Likewise He will raise them on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 10:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever desires honour—to Allah belongs all honour. To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it. But those who plot evil deeds—for them is a severe punishment, and the plotting of those will perish.﴾ (35:10)

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿Whoever desires honour—to Allah belongs all honour﴾. Some of them said: the meaning is: whoever desires honour through worshipping the gods and idols, then indeed honour belongs entirely to Allah.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah ﴿Whoever desires honour﴾, he said: whoever desires honour through worshipping the gods; ﴿then indeed honour belongs entirely to Allah﴾.

Others said: the meaning is, whoever desires honour, let him seek honour through obedience to Allah.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿Whoever desires honour—to Allah belongs all honour﴾, he said: let him seek honour through obedience to Allah.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: whoever desires to know for whom honour is, then it belongs to Allah entirely, meaning every aspect of honour belongs to Allah.

The view that is most correct in my opinion is the view of those who said: whoever desires honour, let him seek it through Allah, for to Allah belongs all honour, apart from everything else besides Him of gods and idols.

I say that this is more correct because the verses preceding this verse were occupied with Allah rebuking the polytheists for their worship of idols, and reproaching them, and threatening them for it. Thus it is more fitting that this verse also be of the same kind, urging them to abandon that, so its context resembles theirs and it is within their setting.

* *

As for His saying ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾:

His saying, may He be remembered, means: to Allah ascends the remembrance of the servant of Him and his praise of Him. ﴿And righteous deed raises it﴾ means: and the servant's righteous deed raises his remembrance of his Lord up to Him, and that is acting in obedience to Him, performing His obligations, and abstaining from what He has commanded.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Awn informed me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah al-Mas'udi, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mukhariq, from his father al-Mukhariq ibn Sulaym, who said: Abd Allah said to us: "When we narrate a hadith to you, we bring you confirmation of it from the Book of Allah: indeed the Muslim servant, when he says: 'Subhan Allah wa-bihamdih, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, Allah akbar, tabaraka Allah,' an angel takes them and places them beneath his wings, then ascends with them to the heaven. He does not pass with them over a company of angels except that they seek forgiveness for their speaker, until with them he reaches the face of the Most Merciful." Then Abd Allah recited ﴿and righteous deed raises it﴾.

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Sa'id al-Jurayri informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, who said: Ka'b said: "Indeed, for 'Subhan Allah,' 'al-hamdu lillah,' 'la ilaha illa Allah,' and 'Allahu akbar,' there is a humming around the Throne like the humming of bees, mentioning their companion; and righteous deed is in the treasuries."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Shahr ibn Hawshab al-Ash'ari, concerning His saying ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it﴾, he said: "Righteous deed raises the good word."

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it﴾, he said: "The good word is the remembrance of Allah, and righteous deed is performing His obligations. Whoever remembers Allah, the Exalted, while performing His obligations, the remembrance of Allah is carried upon him and it ascends with him to Allah. And whoever remembers Allah but does not perform His obligations, his words are returned upon his deed, and it is more fitting for him."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it﴾, he said: "Righteous deed raises the good speech."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it﴾, he said: al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "Allah does not accept a word except with a deed. Whoever speaks and does good deeds, Allah accepts from him."

* *

As for His saying ﴿But those who plot evil deeds﴾:

His saying, may He be remembered, means: those who earn evil deeds, for them is the punishment of Hell.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to me, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿But those who plot evil deeds—for them is a severe punishment﴾, he said: "These are the people of polytheism."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and the plotting of those will perish﴾:

He says: the deeds of these polytheists will perish, so they will be nullified and gone, because it was not for Allah, so it did not benefit its doer.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿and the plotting of those will perish﴾, he said: "it will be corrupted."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, concerning ﴿and the plotting of those will perish﴾, he said: "They are the people of showing off (riya')."

Muhammad ibn Umarah narrated to me, saying: Sahl ibn Abi Amir narrated to us, saying: Ja'far al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, concerning His saying ﴿and the plotting of those will perish﴾, he said: "They are the people of showing off."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿and the plotting of those will perish﴾, he said: "It perished, so it did not benefit them, nor did they benefit from it, and it harmed them."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 11:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then He made you into pairs. No female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. And no one is granted long life or has any of his life shortened except that it is in a Book. Indeed that is easy for Allah.﴾ (35:11)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And Allah created you﴾ O people ﴿from dust﴾, meaning by that that He created your father Adam from dust; so the creation of their father from it was made a creation for them. ﴿Then from a sperm-drop﴾, meaning: then He created you from the sperm-drop of the man and the woman. ﴿Then He made you into pairs﴾, meaning that He paired the female with the male from among you.

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said according to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And Allah created you from dust﴾: meaning Adam; ﴿then from a sperm-drop﴾: meaning his offspring; ﴿then He made you into pairs﴾: so He paired some of you with others.

* *

As for His saying ﴿No female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge﴾:

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: No female among you, O people, conceives any pregnancy or sperm-drop except that He knows her conceiving of it and her delivery of it, and whether it is male or female. Nothing of that is hidden from Him.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And no one is granted long life or has any of his life shortened except that it is in a Book﴾:

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: "No one is granted long life so that his life is prolonged, nor is the life of another man shortened compared to the life of this one who has been granted a long life, ﴿except that it is in a Book﴾ with Him, written before she conceives him in her womb and before she delivers him; He has counted all of that and known it before He created him. Nothing is added to what is written for him, nor subtracted."

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And no one is granted long life...﴾ up to ﴿easy﴾: He says: No one for whom I have decreed a long life and existence will fail to reach what I have decreed for him of life, and I have decreed that for him; it only comes to the Book in which I have decreed for him, nothing being added to it. And no one for whom I have decreed a short life and existence will reach a [longer] life; rather, it comes to the Book in which I have decreed for him, nothing being added to it. That is His saying ﴿and none has any of his life shortened except that it is in a Book﴾; He says: all of that is in a Book with Him.

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Whoever I have decreed for him to live until old age reaches him, or to live less than that, every person reaches his appointed term which has been decreed for him; all of that is in a Book.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And no one is granted long life or has any of his life shortened except that it is in a Book﴾: Do you not see people? A man lives a hundred years, and another dies the moment he is born? This is this. The pronoun in His saying ﴿nor is any of his life shortened﴾ according to this interpretation, although it apparently refers to the name of the first person granted long life, refers to the name of another person besides him. That is acceptable because if its owner were stated explicitly, it would appear in the wording of the first; this is like their saying: "I have a garment and half of it," meaning: half of the other.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "No one is granted long life, nor is any of his life shortened by the passing away of what has passed of the days of his life; that is the shortening of his life." The pronoun in this interpretation refers to the first person granted long life, because the meaning of the statement is: no one's life is prolonged, and nothing is taken from his life, so that it is shortened, except that it is in a Book with Allah, written, counted and known by Him.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Husayn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to me, saying: 'Abthar related to us, saying: Husayn related to us, from Abu Malik regarding this verse ﴿And no one is granted long life or has any of his life shortened except that it is in a Book﴾: He said: what is decreed of his days which have been counted for him, except that it is in a Book.

Of the two interpretations, the more correct in my view is the first, because it is the more apparent of the two meanings and the more consistent with the apparent sense of the revelation.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed that is easy for Allah﴾:

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Indeed, counting the lifespans of His creatures is easy and simple for Him, whether they are long or short; none of it is beyond His capacity.

The Commentary on the Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿And the two seas are not alike: one is sweet, fresh, pleasant to drink, and the other is salty, bitter. From both you eat tender flesh, and you extract ornaments which you wear; and you see the ships ploughing through it, that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will give thanks.﴾ (35:12)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And the two seas are not equal, so they do not become alike: one of them is sweet, fresh (al-Furat), and al-Furat is the sweetest of the sweet; and this is salty, bitter (ujaj)," meaning: the other of them is salty and bitter, and that is the water of the Green Sea (al-Bahr al-Akhdar), and ujaj means bitter, the most saline of waters.

As it was said:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and this is salty, bitter﴾: ujaj means bitter.

* *

As for His words ﴿And from both you eat tender flesh﴾

He says: and from both seas you eat tender flesh, and that is fish, from both of them, the sweet, fresh one and the salty, bitter one. ﴿And you extract ornaments which you wear﴾ meaning: pearls and coral, which you extract from the salty, bitter sea. The manner of ﴿you extract ornaments﴾ has been explained before, and it is extracted from the salt water, in what has passed, in a way that makes its repetition unnecessary. ﴿And you see the ships ploughing through it﴾ He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: and you see the ships in all those seas ploughing the water with their prows, and that is their cleaving of it when one passes through, called mākhira; it is said of it: makhara, yamkhuru, and yamkharu makhran, when it cleaves the water with its prow.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this:

Mention of those who said so:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And from both you eat tender flesh﴾, i.e., from both of them together; ﴿and you extract ornaments which you wear﴾, this is the pearl; ﴿and you see the ships ploughing through it﴾, in it the ships come and go with one wind.

Ali narrated to us, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and you see the ships ploughing through it﴾, he said: "running ships" (jawari).

* *

As for His words ﴿that you may seek of His bounty﴾

He says: that you may seek, by your riding these seas in the ships, your livelihoods, and that you may conduct your trade in them, and give thanks to God for His subjecting that to you, and for what He has provided you from it of good provision and fine ornaments.

The Interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. And those you invoke other than Him do not possess [so much as] a thin membrane (qitmir).﴾ [35:13]

His exalted remembrance says: He makes the night enter the day, meaning that what is lost from the night He causes to enter the day, adding it to it; and He makes the day enter the night, meaning that what is lost from the parts of the day He adds to the parts of the night, causing it to enter them.

As related to us:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night﴾: the increase of this is at the expense of that, and the decrease of that is at the expense of this.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night﴾: he says, it is the diminishing of one of them by the other.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term﴾:

He says: He has made the sun and the moon run for you as a blessing from Him upon you and as a mercy from Him toward you, so that you may know the number of years and the reckoning, and recognize the night from the day.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿each running for a specified term﴾:

He says: all of that runs for a known appointed time.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the like of what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term﴾: a known term, a limit that it neither falls short of nor exceeds.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾:

He says: The One who does these deeds is your worshipped one, O people, the One for whom worship alone is fitting, and He is Allah, your Lord.

As related to us:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion﴾: that is, He is the One who does this.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿to Him belongs dominion﴾:

His exalted remembrance says: to Him belongs complete dominion, such that there is nothing that is not within His dominion and authority.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿And those you invoke other than Him do not possess [so much as] a thin membrane﴾:

His exalted remembrance says: And those you worship, O people, other than your Lord, who has this attribute mentioned in these verses, who has complete dominion, to which no dominion is comparable — their attribute is ﴿they do not possess [so much as] a thin membrane﴾. He says: they do not possess the husk of a date-stone or what is above it.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the like of what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Yaqub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Awf informed us, from one who related to him, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿they do not possess [so much as] a thin membrane﴾: he said, it is the skin of the date-stone.

* 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿[so much as] a thin membrane﴾: he says, the skin that is on the back of the date-stone.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿they do not possess [so much as] a thin membrane﴾: he means the husk of the date-stone.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah ﴿[so much as] a thin membrane﴾: he said, the lining of the date-stone, like the thin film of an egg-shell.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿they do not possess [so much as] a thin membrane﴾: al-qitmir is the thin skin that is on the top of the date-stone.

* 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid related to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah related to us, from Juwaybir, from some of his companions, concerning His saying ﴿they do not possess [so much as] a thin membrane﴾: he said, it is the qima' that is on the date.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu 'Amir related to us, saying: Murrah related to us, from 'Atiyyah, who said: al-qitmir: the husk of the date-stone.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 14:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you call upon them, they will not hear your call; and even if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association (of them with Allah). And none can inform you like one [who is] Acquainted.﴾

His saying ﴿If you call upon them, they will not hear your call; and even if they heard, they would not respond to you﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: If you call upon them, O people, those gods you worship besides Allah, they will not hear your call, because they are inanimate objects that do not understand what you say. ﴿And even if they heard﴾ means: and even if they heard your calling upon them and understood from you that it is your speech, by granting them hearing with which they could hear, ﴿they would not respond to you﴾, because they are not speaking, and no one who hears a speech is able to answer it. He, exalted is His mention, says to the polytheists who associate the gods and idols with Allah: How then can you worship besides Allah one with such attributes, who has no benefit for you with Him and no power to harm you, and leave worship of the One in whose hand is your benefit and harm, who created you and bestowed favors upon you?

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿If you call upon them, they will not hear your call; and even if they heard, they would not respond to you﴾: that is, they would not accept that from you, nor would they benefit you in it.

* *

And His saying ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association (of them with Allah)﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says to the polytheists who worship idols: On the Day of Resurrection your gods that you worship besides Allah will disavow that they were ever partners of Allah in the world.

As:

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association (of them with Allah)﴾: they will not accept them, nor be pleased with them, nor acknowledge it.

* *

And His saying ﴿And none can inform you like one [who is] Acquainted﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: And none can inform you, O Muhammad, about the gods of these polytheists and what will befall them and their worshippers on the Day of Resurrection, of their disavowal of them and their denial of them, like one who has knowledge of their affair and theirs, and that One Acquainted is Allah, to whom nothing is hidden, whether it has existed or will exist, glorified is He.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And none can inform you like one [who is] Acquainted﴾: And Allah is the Acquainted, (who knows) that this will happen from them on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 15–18:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah, and Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy (15)﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: O mankind, you are those in need and poverty before your Lord, so worship Him alone, and hasten toward His good pleasure. He will enrich you from your poverty and grant your needs in His presence. ﴿And Allah is the Self-Sufficient﴾ (al-Ghani), free of your worship of Him and of your service, and free of other things, whether from you or from others. ﴿The Praiseworthy﴾ (al-Hamid) means: the one praised for His blessings, for every blessing upon you and upon others comes from Him, so to Him belong praise and thanks in every state.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation (16). And that is not difficult for Allah (17). No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative. You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen and establish prayer. And whoever purifies himself, purifies himself only for his own soul. And to Allah is the final return (18)﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: If He wills, O people, your Lord can destroy you, for He created you without any need for you. ﴿And bring a new creation﴾ means: and bring about others besides you who obey Him, comply with His command, and refrain from what He has forbidden them.

As [reported]:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation﴾: that is, He would bring others besides you.

* *

And His saying ﴿And that is not difficult for Allah﴾

He says: Your removal and the bringing of others besides you is not difficult for Allah; rather, it is easy and simple for Him. He says: So fear Allah, O people, and obey Him before He does that to you.

* *

And His saying ﴿No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: No sinful soul will bear the sin of another soul other than itself. ﴿And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative﴾ means: If a soul burdened with sins calls upon someone to carry its sins and seeks that, it will not find anyone to carry any part of them, even if the one it asked were a close relative, a father or a brother.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another, and if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative﴾: He says: there will be a burden upon him, and he will find no one to carry any part of his burden.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried﴾, like the verse ﴿No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load﴾, to its sins, ﴿nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative﴾, that is, a near kinsman of it; nothing of its sins will be carried, and it will not be made to carry the sins of others ﴿No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾. The accusative of "close relative" (dha qurba) is the complement of "kana" (was), because the meaning of the statement is: even if the one you ask to carry its sins were a close relative to it. The feminine form of "heavily laden" (muthqalah) is used because the speech has been directed to the soul (nafs), as if it were said: if a soul heavy with sins calls to carry its sins. It was said this way because the word nafs applies to both male and female, as in ﴿Every soul will taste death﴾, meaning every male and female.

* *

And His saying ﴿You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): You can only warn, O Muhammad, those who fear the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection without having witnessed it, but out of faith in what you have brought them and their acceptance of you concerning what you have informed them of from Allah. These are the ones whom your warning benefits and who are admonished by your exhortations, not those upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal, so that they do not understand.

As [reported]:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding the saying ﴿You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen﴾: that is, those who fear the Fire.

* *

And His saying ﴿and establish prayer﴾

He says: they perform the obligatory prayer with its limits, as Allah has prescribed it for them.

* *

And His saying ﴿And whoever purifies himself, purifies himself only for his own soul﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Whoever purifies himself from the filth of disbelief and sins by repenting to Allah, believing in Him, and acting in obedience to Him, purifies himself only for his own soul, for he thereby earns for it the good pleasure of Allah, success in His Gardens, and deliverance from His punishment which He has prepared for those who disbelieve in Him.

As [reported]:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And whoever purifies himself, purifies himself only for his own soul﴾: that is, whoever does righteous deeds, he does them only for himself.

* *

And His saying ﴿And to Allah is the final return﴾

He says: To Allah is the return of every one of you who acts, O people, believer and disbeliever, righteous and wicked, and He will recompense you all for what you have sent forward of good and evil, according to what each has earned.

The interpretation of the Qur'an (ta'wil) has been disputed concerning the meaning of "the Book" that Allah mentions in this verse as having been bequeathed to those whom He chose from among His servants, and who are meant by "those chosen from among His servants," and who is "the one who wrongs himself." Some of them said: The Book is the scriptures that Allah sent down before the Furqan (the Criterion, i.e. the Qur'an). And those chosen from among His servants are the Community of Muhammad (ﷺ). And "the one who wrongs himself" refers to the sinners among them.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words, ﴿Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those whom We have chosen from among Our servants...﴾ up to His words ﴿the great bounty﴾: They are the Community of Muhammad (ﷺ), whom Allah made heirs of every Book He sent down. So their wrongdoer will be forgiven, their moderate one will be reckoned with an easy reckoning, and their foremost in good deeds will enter Paradise without reckoning.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Qays narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Isa, from Yazid ibn al-Harith, from Shaqiq, from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, that he said: This Community is three thirds on the Day of Resurrection: a third will enter Paradise without reckoning, a third will be reckoned with an easy reckoning, and a third will come with great sins, until it is said: "What are these?" — and He is the most knowing, may He be blessed and exalted — and the angels will say: "These came with great sins, except that they did not associate anything with You." The Lord will say: "Admit these into the vastness of My mercy." And Abdullah recited this verse: ﴿Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those whom We have chosen from among Our servants﴾.

Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Awn narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal narrated to us, saying: Ka'b al-Ahbar said that the one who wrongs himself from this Community, and the moderate one, and the foremost in good deeds, are all in Paradise. Have you not seen that Allah said: ﴿Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those whom We have chosen from among Our servants...﴾ up to His words ﴿every ungrateful one﴾.

Ali ibn Sa'id al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Awf, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, who said: I heard Ka'b say, concerning ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission﴾: "They are all in Paradise," and he recited this verse: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter﴾.

al-Hasan ibn Arafah narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari narrated to us, from Awf ibn Abi Jamilah, who said: Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal narrated to us, saying: Ka'b said that the one who wrongs himself from this Community, and the moderate one, and the foremost in good deeds, are all in Paradise. Have you not seen that Allah said: ﴿Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those whom We have chosen from among Our servants...﴾ up to His words ﴿fatigue﴾, and ﴿As for those who disbelieve, for them is the fire of Hell﴾? He said: Ka'b said: "These are the people of the Fire."

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Awf, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn al-Harith say: Ka'b said: The one who wrongs himself, the moderate one, and the foremost in good deeds from this Community are all in Paradise. Have you not seen that Allah says: ﴿Then We gave the Book as an inheritance...﴾ until He reached His words ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter﴾.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Humayd informed us, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from his father, that Ibn Abbas asked Ka'b about the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those whom We have chosen from among Our servants...﴾ up to His words ﴿by Allah's permission﴾. He said: Amr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, who said: "It is a Community that is shown mercy. The wrongdoer is forgiven, the moderate one is in the gardens with Allah, and the foremost in good deeds is in the high ranks with Allah."

Others said: The Book which Allah gave as an inheritance to these people is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. Those chosen are the Community of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the one among them who wrongs himself is the hypocrite, who is in the Fire, while the moderate one and the foremost in good deeds are in Paradise.

Qatadah said: "People had three ranks in this world, three ranks at death, and three ranks in the Hereafter. As for this world, they were: a believer [[This is an implied subject supplied before it, i.e. they are: a believer... etc., or some of them are believers.]], a hypocrite, and a polytheist. As for at death, Allah said: ﴿But if he is of those brought near, then rest and provision and a Garden of bliss. And if he is of the companions of the right hand, then, "Peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand." And if he is of the deniers, the astray, then a welcome of boiling water and burning in Hellfire﴾ [56:88-94]. And in the Hereafter, they will be three pairs: ﴿So the companions of the right hand — what are the companions of the right hand? And the companions of the left hand — what are the companions of the left hand? And the foremost, the foremost; those are the ones brought near﴾."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those whom We have chosen from among Our servants. Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾: "They are the companions of the left hand. ﴿And among them is one who is moderate﴾: the companions of the right hand. ﴿And among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾: they are the foremost among all people."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those whom We have chosen from among Our servants. Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾: "This one is dropped. ﴿And among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission﴾: this one has outstripped in good deeds, and this one is moderate, following in his footsteps."

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is the interpretation of the one who said that by His words ﴿Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those whom We have chosen from among Our servants﴾ is meant the scriptures that were sent down before the Furqan.

If someone says: How can this be its meaning, when the Community of Muhammad (ﷺ) recites only its own Book and acts only by what is in it of rulings and laws? It is said: The meaning of that is other than what you have proposed. Rather, its meaning is: Then We gave the inheritance of faith in the Book to those whom We have chosen. Among them are believers in every Book Allah sent down from heaven before their Book, and who act by it; for every Book sent down from heaven before the Furqan commands acting by the Furqan when it is revealed, and following the one who brought it. And that is the action of one who affirms Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought, and acts by what he called to, in the Qur'an and in the other Books sent down before it.

It is said that by His words ﴿Then We gave the Book﴾ is meant the Books we mentioned, because the Mighty One, whose praise is great, said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what was before it﴾. Then He followed that with His words ﴿Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those whom We have chosen﴾. It was known, since the meaning of inheritance is only the transfer of something from one people to others, and there was no community in the time of our Prophet (ﷺ) to which a Book had been transferred from a people who were before them other than his Community, that this is its meaning. Since that is so, it is clear that those chosen from among His servants are the believers of his Community. As for the one who wrongs himself, it is more fitting to the meaning of the verse, in my view, that he be one of the people of sins and disobedience which fall short of hypocrisy and polytheism, rather than a hypocrite or disbeliever. That is because Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, followed this verse with His words ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter﴾, thereby including all three categories in entry into Paradise.

If someone says: But His words ﴿which they will enter﴾ refer only to the moderate one and the foremost! It is said to him: What is your proof that this is so, from report or reason? If he says: The established proof that the wrongdoer from this Community will enter the Fire, and if none of these three categories entered the Fire, it would follow that the people of faith have no threat: It is said: There is no report in the verse that they will not enter the Fire. Rather, it reports from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, that they will enter the Gardens of Eden. It is possible that the one who wrongs himself enters it after Allah's punishment for his sins which he committed in this world, and his wronging of himself in them, by the Fire or by whatever punishment Allah wills, and then He admits him to Paradise. He will then be among those whom the report of Allah, the Mighty One, whose praise is great, encompasses with His words ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter﴾.

Reports have been transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) similar to what we have said on this matter; although there is scrutiny in their chains, the Book's evidence supports their soundness in the manner I have explained.

Mention of the report transmitted on this:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, who said: Abu Thabit mentioned that he entered the mosque and sat beside Abu al-Darda', and said: "O Allah, console my loneliness, have mercy on my estrangement, and grant me a righteous companion." Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, that he heard a man from Thaqif narrate from a man from Kinanah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said concerning this verse: (Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those whom We have chosen from among Our servants. By His words ﴿those whom We have chosen from among Our servants﴾ is meant those whom We chose for Our obedience and selected. His words ﴿by Allah's permission﴾ mean: by Allah's enabling him to do so.

His words ﴿That is the great bounty﴾

The Mighty One, whose remembrance is exalted, means: This foremost one who outstripped others in good deeds, by Allah's permission, is the great bounty by which He favored the one who fell short of his rank in obedience to Allah, from among the moderate one and the one who wrongs himself.

As for His words: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief﴾

The interpreters have differed concerning the grief from which these people praised Allah for removing them. Some said: it is the grief they were in before entering Paradow, from fear of the Fire, as they were fearful that they would enter it.

Those who said that:

⁕ Qatadah ibn Sa'id ibn Qatadah al-Sadusi related to me, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham, the companion of al-Dastawa'i, related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Amr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief﴾, he said: the grief of the Fire.

Rather, their hearts are sound, but there entered into them such fear as did not enter others, and their knowledge of the Hereafter prevented them from the world. So they said, "Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief." By Allah, their grief was not the grief of this world, nor did what they sought to attain Paradise become great in their own souls. Fear of the Fire made them weep, and whoever is not consoled by the consolation of Allah will cut his soul to pieces in regret over this world, and whoever does not see a blessing of Allah upon him except in food or drink has little knowledge and his punishment is near.

Others said: it refers to death.

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from his father, from Ata', regarding His words ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief﴾, he said: death.

Others said: it refers to the grief of the toil they endured in the world.

Those who said that:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief"﴾, he said: In the world they used to work and toil while in fear, or they grieved.

Others said: rather, it refers to the grief that befalls the one who wronged himself on the Day of Standing.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, who said: Abu Thabit mentioned that Abu al-Darda' said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "As for the one who wronged himself, he will be afflicted in that place with distress and grief, and that is His words ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief﴾."

He, exalted is He, says: Thus does He requite every one who denies the blessings of his Lord on the Day of Resurrection, by making them enter the Fire of Hell for their evil deeds which they sent ahead in the world.

* *

He, exalted is He, says: These disbelievers will cry for help and wail in the Fire, saying: "O our Lord, bring us out, we will do righteousness," meaning: we will act in obedience to You, "other than what we used to do" before, of Your disobedience.
