As for His words, "Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one":

He, exalted is He, says: Thus does He requite every one who denies the blessings of his Lord on the Day of Resurrection, by making them enter the Fire of Hell for their evil deeds which they sent ahead in the world.

* *

As for His words, "They will cry out therein, 'Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteousness, other than what we used to do'":

He, exalted is He, says: These disbelievers will cry for help and wail in the Fire, saying: "O our Lord, bring us out, we will do righteousness," meaning: we will act in obedience to You, "other than what we used to do" before, of Your disobedience. The word "yastarikhun" (they cry out) is of the form "yaftaʿilun" from "al-sarakh" (crying out); its "ta" was changed to "ta" (ṭāʾ) because its point of articulation is close to the "sad" when it became heavy.

* *

As for His words, "Did We not give you life enough for whoever would remember to remember therein":

The interpreters differed regarding the extent of that. Some of them said: it is forty years.

Those who said that:

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: "The life span in which Allah has left the son of Adam without excuse, 'Did We not give you life enough for whoever would remember to remember therein,'" is forty years.

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, that he used to say: When one of you reaches forty years, let him take his caution from Allah.

Others said: rather, it is sixty years.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "Did We not give you life enough for whoever would remember to remember therein": he said: sixty years.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, say: The life span in which Allah has left the son of Adam without excuse is sixty years.

Ali ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, from Abu Husayn al-Makki, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, a call will be made: 'Where are the sons of sixty?' – and that is the life span of which Allah said, 'Did We not give you life enough for whoever would remember to remember therein, and the warner had come to you?'"

Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Himsi narrated to me, saying: Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Mutarrif ibn Mazin al-Kinani narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar ibn Rashid narrated to me, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ghifari say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has left the one who reaches sixty or seventy years without excuse."

Abu Salih al-Fazari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sawwar narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Abd al-Qari al-Iskandarani narrated to us, saying: Abu Hazim narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever Allah grants life for sixty years has left no excuse for himself regarding his lifespan."

Muhammad ibn Sawwar narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Tarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding His words, "Did We not give you life enough for whoever would remember to remember therein, and the warner had come to you," he said: The life span with which Allah gave you life is sixty years.

The more fitting of the two sayings to the interpretation of the verse, since the report we have mentioned from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has in its chain someone whose transmission must be scrutinized, is the saying of those who said it is forty years, because at forty a person's intellect and understanding reach their maturity, and what comes before and after that is deficient from its completeness in the state of forty.

* *

As for His words, "and the warner had come to you":

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of "the warner." Some of them said: it refers to Muhammad (ﷺ).

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, "and the warner had come to you": "The warner is the Prophet," and he recited, "This is a warner of the warners of old" (53:56).

And it was said: it refers to white hair (gray hair).

So the meaning of the statement, then, is: Did We not give you life, O assembly of polytheists with Allah from Quraysh, for years in which whoever has understanding and intellect would be reminded, and whoever would be admonished among them would be admonished, and whoever would repent would repent, and a warner from Allah had come to you warning you of what you are in today of the torment of Allah? Yet you did not heed the admonitions of Allah, and you did not accept from the warner of Allah who came to you what he brought to you from your Lord.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 38:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ (38)

Says He, the Exalted, Who is mentioned: ﴿Then taste[it]﴾ the fire of the punishment of Hell, which you have burned in, O disbelievers in Allah. ﴿So there is not for the wrongdoers any helper.﴾ That is: there is not for the disbelievers, who wronged themselves and earned for themselves the anger of Allah by their disbelief in Allah in the world, any helper who would help them against Allah to rescue them from His punishment.

* *

And His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾

Says He, the Exalted, Who is mentioned: Indeed, Allah knows what you, O people, conceal and hide within yourselves, and what you have not hidden or intended but will intend later, and what is absent from your sight in the heavens and the earth. So fear Him lest He look upon you while you harbor within yourselves doubt about the oneness of Allah or about the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), other than what you show with your tongues. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 39:

The interpretation of the words of the Most High: ﴿It is He who has made you successors (khala'if) upon the earth. So whoever disbelieves, his disbelief is upon himself, and the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them in the sight of their Lord except in hatred (maqtan), and the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them except in loss.﴾ (35:39)

The Most High says: It is Allah who has made you, O people, successors upon the earth after ʿAad and Thamud, and after those nations that passed away before you; so He has made you succeed them in their dwellings and their homes.

As related by:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿It is He who has made you successors upon the earth﴾: a nation after a nation, and a generation after a generation.

* * *

And as for His words ﴿So whoever disbelieves, his disbelief is upon himself﴾:

The Most High says: So whoever among you, O people, disbelieves in Allah, the harm of his disbelief falls upon himself; he harms no one else by it, because he is the one who will be punished for it, not anyone other than him.

* * *

And as for His words ﴿And the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them in the sight of their Lord except in hatred﴾:

The Most High says: The disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them in the sight of their Lord except in distance from the mercy of Allah. ﴿And the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them except in loss﴾: he says, the disbelief of the disbelievers in Allah does not increase them except in destruction.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 40:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Have you considered your partners whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? Or have We given them a book so that they are upon clear evidence from it?" Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion.﴾ (35:40)

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people, ﴿"Have you considered"﴾, O people, ﴿your partners whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me ﴿what they have created from the earth﴾﴾, meaning: show me what thing they have created from the earth. ﴿Or do they have a share in the heavens?﴾, meaning: or do your partners have a share with Allah in the heavens, if they have not created anything from the earth? ﴿Or have We given them a book so that they are upon clear evidence from it?﴾, meaning: or have We given these polytheists a book that We sent down to them from the sky, commanding them to associate idols and images with Allah, so that they are upon evidence from it, that is, upon proof for what I have commanded them in regard to associating others with Me?

Those who hold the same view as we have stated concerning this are the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil).

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Say, "Have you considered your partners whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth"﴾: "Nothing. By Allah, they created nothing from it." ﴿Or do they have a share in the heavens?﴾: "No, by Allah, they have no share in them." (Or have We given them a book so that they are upon clear evidence from it?) meaning: Or have We given them a book that commands them to associate others with Allah?

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion﴾:

This is the saying of some of them to others: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position﴾ (39:3), as deception from some of them toward others and delusion. Indeed, their gods bring them closer to the Fire and push them away from Allah and His mercy.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 41:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease [from their places]. And if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth﴾ lest they cease from their places. ﴿And if they should cease﴾ means: if they were to cease, ﴿no one could hold them after Him﴾ means: no one other than Him could hold them. The particle "la'in" in His words ﴿And if they should cease﴾ has been placed in the position of "law" (if/were), because both are followed by one and the same answer, so they resemble each other in meaning. A parallel to this is His words ﴿And if We were to send a wind and they saw it turned yellow, they would surely continue to disbelieve after it﴾, meaning: even if We were to send a wind. And as He said ﴿And if you were to bring to those who were given the Scripture﴾, meaning: if you were to bring. We have already explained this earlier in a way that suffices and need not be repeated here.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease﴾: from their places.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, who said: A man came to Abdullah and said: "Where have you come from?" He said: "From al-Sham." He said: "Whom did you meet?" He said: "I met Ka'b." He said: "What did Ka'b tell you?" He said: "He told me that the heavens revolve on the shoulder of an angel." He said: "Did you believe him or did you deny him?" He said: "I neither believed him nor denied him." He said: "I wish you had ransomed your journey to him with your mount and its saddle. Ka'b lied. Indeed Allah says ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him﴾."

* Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: Jundab al-Bajali went to Ka'b al-Ahbar, and came to him, then returned. Abdullah said to him: "Tell us what he told you." He said: "He told me that the sky is on a pivot like the pivot of a millstone, and the pivot is a pillar upon the shoulder of an angel." Abdullah said: "I wish you had ransomed your journey with a mount like his." Then he said: "Jewishness has been knotted into the heart of a servant, and it nearly departed from him." Then he said: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease﴾: "It is enough for their ceasing that they revolve."

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed Allah is Forbearing toward those among His creatures who associate others with Him and disbelieve in Him, in that He delays hastening His punishment upon them, and Forgiving of the sins of those among them who repent and turn back in faith in Him and act in a way that pleases Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 42–43:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And they swore by Allah with their most solemn oaths that if a warner came to them, they would surely be better guided than any (other) of the nations. But when a warner came to them, it only increased them in aversion, in arrogance on the earth and evil plotting. But evil plotting does not beset anyone except its own planners. So do they await anything but the way of the former peoples? You will not find any change in the way of Allah, and you will not find any alteration in the way of Allah.﴾

His, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These polytheists swore by Allah with their most solemn oaths, meaning: with the strongest of oaths, and they went to great lengths in them: "If a warner comes to them from Allah, one who warns them of the punishment of Allah, ﴿they would surely be better guided than any (other) of the nations﴾," meaning: they would surely be more upright in the path of truth and more ready to accept what the warner brings them from Allah, more than any of the nations that passed before them. ﴿But when a warner came to them﴾, by the warner is meant Muhammad ﷺ, meaning: when Muhammad came to them, warning them of Allah's punishment for their disbelief.

As:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿But when a warner came to them﴾, that he is Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

And His words ﴿it only increased them in aversion﴾

He says: the coming of the warner increased them only in aversion and flight from faith in Allah, following the truth, and taking the path of guidance.

* *

And His words ﴿in arrogance on the earth﴾

He says: they fled in arrogance on the earth and in evil deception, because they turned the weak away from following him while they disbelieved in him. And the plotting here is shirk.

As:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and evil plotting﴾, that it is shirk. The plotting has been attributed to "evil" (al-sayyi'), and "evil" is a qualifier of the plotting, as it is said ﴿Indeed, this is the true certainty (haqq al-yaqin)﴾. It has also been said that in the reading of Abdullah it is ﴿and plotting, evil﴾ (makran sayyi'an), and in this is confirmation of the statement we have made, that "evil" in meaning is a qualifier of the plotting. The readers of the regional centres, other than al-A'mash and Hamzah, read it with a moved hamzah in the genitive case (sayyi'i). Al-A'mash and Hamzah read it with a hamzah and a sukun on the hamzah, on the grounds that when vowels accumulate in this, it becomes heavy, so they made the hamzah quiescent, as the poet said:

"When they become crooked, I say: O companion, straighten (them)."[[The verse is among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Quran (folio 267). He said: And His words "makr al-sayyi'" (the plotting of the evil): the plotting is attributed to the evil, and it is the same thing, as He said "Indeed, this is the true certainty." Confirmation of this is in the reading of Abdullah: "makran sayyi'an." And His words "makr al-sayyi'": the hamzah in "sayyi'" is in the genitive, and al-A'mash and Hamzah made it quiescent because of the number of vowels, as He said "the great terror will not grieve them"; the poet said: "When they become crooked, I say: O companion, straighten (them)." He means: "O companion of a people," so he made the ba' quiescent because of the number of vowels. Al-Farra' said: Al-Rawasi related to me, from Abu Amr ibn al-Ala': "la yahzunahum" with a jazm (quiescent), end.]]

So he made the ba' quiescent because of the number of vowels.

The correct reading is that of the regional readers, which is to move the hamzah in it to the genitive. It is not permissible in the Qur'an to recite it in every way that is permissible in Arabic, because recitation is only what the earlier imams recited and what the predecessors transmitted in the manner they received from those before them.

* *

And His words ﴿But evil plotting does not beset anyone except its own planners﴾

He says: the evil plotting does not descend except upon its people, meaning upon those who plot it, and He only meant that the harm of that plotting which these polytheists plotted does not befall anyone but themselves.

Qatadah said concerning this, as related:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿But evil plotting does not beset anyone except its own planners﴾, that it is shirk.

* *

And His words ﴿So do they await anything but the way of the former peoples?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So do these polytheists among your people, O Muhammad, await anything but Allah's way with them in the immediate life of this world for their disbelief in Him, a painful punishment; meaning: do these await anything but that I inflict upon them, from My vengeance for their associating others with Me and their denying My messenger, the like of what I inflicted upon those before them of their likes among the nations.

As:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿So do they await anything but the way of the former peoples?﴾, i.e., the punishment of the former peoples. ﴿You will not find any change in the way of Allah﴾, meaning: you will not find, O Muhammad, any alteration in the way of Allah.

* *

And His words ﴿and you will not find any alteration in the way of Allah﴾

He says: you will not find in His creation any alteration of His way. He says: that will not change or alter it, because there is no repelling of His decree.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 44:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not travelled in the earth and seen how was the end of those before them, though they were greater than them in strength? Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth. Indeed, He is ever Knowing and Competent.﴾

His saying, exalted is His mention: Have these polytheists not travelled, O Muhammad, in the earth whose people We destroyed for their disbelief in Us and their denial of Our messengers? Indeed, they are merchants who take the route to Syria. ﴿So they could observe how was the end of those before them⦁﴾ from the nations through whose lands they used to pass. Did We not destroy them, ruin their dwellings, and make them an example for those who came after them, so that they would take warning from them, desist from what they were upon of worshipping idols by associating others with Allah, and know that the One who did to those what He did is able to do to them the like of what He did to those, hastening retribution and punishment upon them? ﴿And they were greater than them in strength⦁﴾ it will not be difficult for Him to do to them the like of what He did to those, by hastening vengeance and punishment upon them.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said concerning His saying ﴿and they were greater than them in strength﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and they were greater than them in strength⦁﴾: it informs you that He gave those people what He did not give you.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth⦁﴾

His saying, exalted is His mention: These polytheists who worship idols and deny Muhammad will not frustrate Us, so that they outrun Us in flight on the earth when We wish to destroy them; for Allah is not such that anything He wills in the heavens or on the earth can frustrate Him, and these polytheists will not be able to escape from the regions of the heavens and the earth.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, He is ever Knowing and Competent⦁﴾

His saying, exalted is His mention: Indeed, Allah is Knowing of His creation, of what is to occur, and of who among them deserves the hastening of punishment, and who among them, away from his misguidance, will return to guidance and repent; Competent to take vengeance on whomever He wills among them, and to grant success to whomever He wills among them to believe.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if Allah were to take mankind to task for what they have earned, He would not leave upon it [the earth] a single creature﴾ [35:45].

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And if Allah were to take mankind to task﴾, meaning: and if Allah were to punish and requite mankind for the sins and disobediences they committed and the transgressions they perpetrated, ﴿He would not leave upon it [its back] a single creature that walks upon it﴾. ﴿But He defers them until a specified term﴾, meaning: but He defers their punishment and their being taken to task for what they earned until a term known to Him, determined and limited, from which they cannot fall short and which they cannot exceed once they reach it.

The commentators have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And if Allah were to take mankind to task for what they have earned, He would not leave upon it a single creature﴾: except what Noah carried in the Ark.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So when their term comes, then indeed Allah is ever, of His servants, Seeing﴾.

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be exalted: So when the time of their punishment comes, then indeed Allah is ever Seeing of His servants, of who deserves to be punished among them, who deserves honor, who among them was obedient to Him in the world, and who among them was a polytheist in it. Not one of them is hidden from Him, and the knowledge of nothing of their affairs escapes Him.

End of the commentary on Surah Fatir.
